Zotero group IAS

Published

15 October 2026

This report shows the state of the Zotero group IAS (open the group in Zotero). It gives an overview of the literature in the group, and lists the items which should be corrected.

Each item in the lists can be opened in the Zotero web library or in the Zotero app on your computer, so that it can be corrected directly. Corrected items disappear from the lists the next time the report is updated. Some checks compare the items with OpenAlex, an open catalogue of scholarly publications.

Items to fix

The lists are sorted by importance. Use the search field above a list to find an item. web opens the item in the Zotero web library, app in the Zotero app.

Retracted publications

These publications have been retracted. Check whether they should still be cited, and mark or remove them in Zotero.

DOI points to a different publication

The DOI of these items leads to a publication with a different title or year. Usually the DOI is wrong: open the DOI to see where it leads, and correct it in Zotero. Differences of one year (e.g. published online before print) are not listed.

Items which are in the group more than once

These items are in the group more than once, with the same DOI, or with the same title, year and first author. Keep one copy and merge or delete the others, e.g. with Duplicate Items in the Zotero app.

DOI field with an invalid DOI

The DOI field of these items contains something which is not a valid DOI. Correct or remove it.

DOI field with a link or prefix instead of the DOI

The DOI field of these items contains the DOI as a link (https://doi.org/…) or with a prefix (DOI …). Citation styles add the link themselves, so it would appear twice. Replace it with the DOI only.

DOI in the wrong field

These items have no DOI in the DOI field, but a DOI in the URL or Extra field. Copy the DOI into the DOI field. If the item type has no DOI field, the DOI is fine in Extra.

DOI not found in OpenAlex

These DOIs were not found in OpenAlex. The DOI may be wrong: open it to check. If it leads to the right publication, the publication is simply not (yet) in OpenAlex and nothing needs to be done.

Missing or unusual publication year

These items have no date, a date from which no year could be read, or a year in the future. Correct the date in Zotero.

Empty journal, volume, issue or pages, found in OpenAlex

These journal articles have an empty journal, volume, issue or pages field, and OpenAlex has the value for their DOI. Check it with the DOI and fill in the field.

Language not given as a language code

The language of these items is not given as a language code (en, fr, en-US), e.g. as English or eng. Citation styles only recognise the codes. Where the language was recognised, the code is shown; otherwise look up the code in the ISO 639-1 list.

Items without DOI, ISBN, ISSN or URL

Readers cannot easily find these items. Add a DOI, ISBN, ISSN or URL if one exists. Some items, e.g. personal communications, have none.

Items without DOI, for which OpenAlex has one

OpenAlex was searched by title for items without a DOI (journal articles, books, book sections, reports, conference papers, theses, preprints). The publications found are compared by title, year and first author: a likely match agrees in all three, a possible match has a similar title, but e.g. a different year or author. Open the DOI to check that it is the same publication, and add the DOI in Zotero.

Items without tags

These items have no tags. This only matters if the group uses tags, e.g. to assign items to chapters.

How the checks work

NoteDetails of the checks

identifiers

DOI coverage (met_id_doi)

Number and share of items with a valid DOI, and items whose DOI field is filled but contains no valid DOI. DOIs are extracted with openalexPro::extract_doi() and lower cased.

ISBN coverage (met_id_isbn)

Number and share of items with an ISBN, overall and for the item types which should have one (book, bookSection).

ISSN coverage (met_id_issn)

Number and share of items with an ISSN, overall and for the item types which should have one (journalArticle, magazineArticle).

DOIs in the wrong field (met_id_doi_misplaced)

Items with an empty DOI field but a DOI in the Url or Extra field. These DOIs are not used for the OpenAlex lookup and should be moved to the DOI field.

DOIs in the wrong form (met_id_doi_form)

Items whose DOI field contains a valid DOI, but not as a bare DOI: as a link (https://doi.org/10.…), with a prefix (doi:, DOI), URL-encoded (%5B for [) or with spaces or other characters around it. Citation styles add the link themselves, so a link in the DOI field appears twice in a bibliography. The bare DOI is the one recognised by openalexPro::extract_doi(), keeping its upper and lower case.

Items without identifier (met_id_none)

Items with none of DOI, ISBN, ISSN or Url. These items can neither be checked against OpenAlex nor easily be retrieved by readers.

DOIs found in OpenAlex for items without a DOI (met_id_candidates)

For items without a DOI, OpenAlex was searched by title (see [get_doi_candidates()]). The works found are compared with the item: title (ignoring case and punctuation), year and the surname of the first author. A work is a likely match if the titles are (nearly) the same (similarity at least 0.95), the years differ by at most 1 and the first authors have the same surname (year or author are not compared if the item has none), and the title has at least 4 words (short titles like “Zoonoses” are too general). It is a possible match if the titles are similar (at least 0.8). Only the best work with a DOI is kept per item. A likely match is only proposed if no other likely match has a different DOI, and if the DOI is not used by another item in the group (which would make it a duplicate).

metadata

Filled fields per item type (met_meta_fields)

Percentage of items with a filled field, per item type, for the main fields: Title, Author, Publication Year, Publication Title, Publisher, DOI, ISBN, ISSN, Url, Abstract Note and Language. Not every field is expected for every item type, e.g. reports have no Publication Title.

Problematic publication years (met_meta_year)

Items whose date is missing (missing), from whose date Zotero could not derive a year (unparseable), or whose year lies in the future (future).

Duplicate items (met_meta_duplicates)

Items which are in the group more than once, identified by the same DOI, or by the same normalised title (lower case, letters and digits only), publication year and first word of the first author.

Language not given as a standard code (met_meta_language)

Items whose language is not given as a standard language code, i.e. a two-letter ISO 639-1 code, optionally with a region (en, en-US), but e.g. as a name (English), a three-letter code (eng) or in a different spelling (EN, en_us). Citation styles and other tools only recognise the codes. Where the value is recognised, the standard code is proposed, based on the ISO 639-2 list (R package ISOcodes): codes, three-letter codes and the English names of the languages. Other values, e.g. names in the language itself, several languages or other text, are listed without a proposal.

openalex_check

Zotero DOIs found in OpenAlex (met_check_found)

Valid Zotero DOIs which were / were not found in OpenAlex. A DOI which is not found is either not indexed by OpenAlex or wrong.

Retracted works (met_check_retracted)

Works flagged as retracted by OpenAlex, with the key of the Zotero item(s) with the same DOI.

Wrong DOIs (met_check_mismatch)

Items whose DOI points in OpenAlex to a work with a different title or year, which usually means that the wrong DOI is attached to the item. An item is flagged when the title similarity (normalised Levenshtein distance) is below 0.8 or the years differ by more than one.

Item type agreement (met_check_type)

Zotero item type compared with the OpenAlex work type for items with the same DOI.

Missing dates found in OpenAlex (met_check_date)

Items without a date whose DOI was found in OpenAlex: the publication date in OpenAlex is proposed. OpenAlex gives 1 January when only the year is known, so such dates are proposed as the year only. Items whose DOI points to a different publication are left out.

Empty fields found in OpenAlex (met_check_fill)

Journal articles with an empty journal, volume, issue or pages field whose DOI was found in OpenAlex with these details: the values in OpenAlex are proposed. The journal is only taken if the publication is in a journal in OpenAlex (not e.g. a repository). Items whose DOI points to a different publication are left out.

profile

Publication years (met_prof_year)

Number of items per publication year, with cumulative counts. Items without a year are counted as NA.

Open access status (met_prof_oa)

OpenAlex open access status (gold, diamond, green, hybrid, bronze, closed) of the works, overall and per publication year.

Top journals (met_prof_journals)

The 50 most frequent journals, from the Publication Title in Zotero and the source of the primary location in OpenAlex. Ties at rank 50 are included.

Author countries (met_prof_countries)

Number of works with at least one author affiliated with an institution in a country, per country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes from OpenAlex).

Item types and grey literature (met_prof_types)

Number of items per item type (Zotero) or work type (OpenAlex), and the share of grey literature, i.e. reports, theses, dissertations, web pages, documents, presentations, manuscripts, blog posts and preprints.

Languages (met_prof_language)

Languages as entered, and normalised to two letter codes (lower case, region removed, English spellings mapped to en). Inconsistent codes in the language as entered are a quality issue in themselves.

maintenance

Group activity (met_maint_activity)

Items added per month, and items added / modified in the 30 days before the metrics were calculated.

Items without tags (met_maint_tags)

Items without manual tags. Automatic tags, e.g. keywords imported from the publisher, are ignored.
